title: X Feed Digest
summary: The feed kept pushing toward persistent agents rather than smarter chat: Gemini Spark, Codex workflow upgrades, and identity-and-memory commentary all pointed to AI that keeps context and works in the background.

Evaluation and operating discipline are getting sharper too. DeepSWE tried to separate agentic coding models on real software tasks, while developer chatter kept focusing on continuity, history search, and the hidden cost of cleaning up AI-written code.
The most interesting enterprise signal was budgetary: one CEO reportedly replaced a $600K Salesforce contract with a vibe-coded CRM and expects much of internal SaaS spend to get compressed next.

The clearest business-news story was SpaceX widening its footprint on two fronts at once: American Airlines plans to adopt Starlink in-flight internet, and the U.S. Space Force awarded a $2.29B military data-network contract.

Outside AI, the most genuinely useful post in the batch was simple consumer-defense advice: if a rental-car company claims hidden damage after return, ask for the inspection paperwork before arguing about the contract.

items.title: @serenaa_ge: DeepSWE Agentic Coding Benchmark
items.body: Serena Ge introduced DeepSWE, a benchmark aimed at agentic coding workflows rather than leaderboard trivia. The point is that models which look similar on public evals can separate much more clearly when measured against day-to-day software tasks.

items.title: @CodexReleases: Codex CLI 0.134.0
items.body: Codex CLI 0.134.0 adds local conversation-history search, unifies profile selection across CLI/TUI/sandbox, and expands MCP support with per-server env targeting, OAuth, and concurrent read-only tools. It's a meaningful usability upgrade for long-running coding workflows.

items.title: @GeminiApp: Spark as a 24/7 Agent
items.body: Google pitched Gemini Spark as a background agent that keeps working after you leave and checks back before major actions. It reinforces the biggest product shift in the feed: competition is moving from one-shot chat answers toward trustworthy delegated execution.

items.title: @kylegawley: AI Code Backlash Warning
items.body: Kyle Gawley joked that AI may write nearly all code in 2026 and a much smaller share in 2027 once teams feel the cleanup burden. The line is funny, but the warning is real: generation is cheap, maintenance debt isn't.

items.title: @elonmusk: Starlink on American Airlines
items.body: American Airlines says it will bring Starlink-powered connectivity to flights starting in 2027, a notable distribution win for SpaceX in consumer internet. If performance holds up, it also puts more pressure on legacy in-flight Wi‑Fi vendors.

items.title: @zerohedge: $2.29B Space Force Contract
items.body: A Space Force award worth $2.29B for a military space data network underlines how much of SpaceX's upside is now defense and communications infrastructure, not just launches. That's a real contract headline with business implications, not just product buzz.

items.title: @HarryStebbings: AI as SaaS Budget Pressure
items.body: Harry Stebbings relayed a CEO claim that a vibe-coded CRM replaced a $600K Salesforce contract in three weeks and that most internal SaaS could disappear next. Even with anecdotal caveats, it's a sharp signal that AI budgets may cannibalize software vendors rather than simply layer on top.

items.title: @heynavtoor: Rental Car Dispute Playbook
items.body: Nav Toor's rental-car anecdote was refreshingly practical: when a company claims hidden damage after drop-off, ask for the inspection report and check-in sheet instead of debating the generic contract language. In his case, that was enough to make an $1,800 charge disappear.

items.title: @urbit: Personal AI Needs Identity & Memory
items.body: Urbit argued that the next personal-AI bottleneck is not raw model intelligence but durable identity, memory, permissions, and ownership. That's a useful frame: assistants don't feel truly personal until they can remember, act, and stay bounded on infrastructure the user controls.
